name: Imam Khomeini International Airport
before:
The thing to get right when booking Tehran is that the city has two airports and they do not overlap. Every international flight uses Imam Khomeini, 35 km south west of the city, and every domestic flight uses Mehrabad. A client connecting from an international arrival onto an internal Iranian flight has to cross Tehran by road between the two.

The airport covers 13,400 hectares with two terminals and two runways, and it is a hub for several carriers. By the financial year ending March 2019 it ranked third in Iran for passenger traffic.

Its opening was not straightforward. It was planned before the 1979 revolution, when Mehrabad was already congested, and was due to open in May 2004 under a Turkish and Austrian consortium. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps shut it down days after the first landing, citing security fears about foreigners running the airport. It reopened in April 2005 with four Iranian airlines.
after:
Tehran's international airport, about 35 km south west of the city. Domestic flights use Mehrabad instead. On its first day of operations, in May 2004, the military blocked the runway and closed it.

Iran closed its airspace after the United States and Israel struck the country on 28 February 2026. International flights resumed here in April, but Iranian airspace can still close at short notice, and European regulators tell their airlines not to fly in it at any altitude.

New US sanctions from 23 September 2026 are aimed at shutting Iranian airlines out of international flying, and Turkish Airlines has suspended its Iran flights until at least March 2027.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran, and the US government tells its citizens not to travel there for any reason.

claims.claim: two airports that do not overlap
claims.wasBefore: The thing to get right when booking Tehran is that the city has two airports and they do not overlap.
claims.why: Framing sentence; reworded to the two-source facts that follow.

claims.claim: every international flight uses IKA, every domestic flight Mehrabad
claims.wasBefore: Every international flight uses Imam Khomeini, 35 km south west of the city, and every domestic flight uses Mehrabad.
claims.why: Absolute dropped: Wikipedia says Hajj and Umrah flights stayed at Mehrabad. Kept as Tehran's international airport, domestic flights at Mehrabad.

claims.claim: connecting passengers cross Tehran by road
claims.wasBefore: A client connecting from an international arrival onto an internal Iranian flight has to cross Tehran by road between the two.
claims.why: An inference with no source of its own, and not strictly true: Wikipedia says Metro Line 1 serves the airport. Moot while the FCDO advises against all travel.

claims.claim: 13,400 hectares, two terminals, two runways, hub for several carriers
claims.wasBefore: The airport covers 13,400 hectares with two terminals and two runways, and it is a hub for several carriers.
claims.why: Area, terminals and hubs rest on Wikipedia alone: the operator's site (ikac.ir), Mehr News and the Financial Tribune all timed out, and the web archive is blocked by the proxy. Two runways is confirmed by OurAirports but was not worth a sentence alone.

claims.claim: third in Iran, year to March 2019
claims.wasBefore: By the financial year ending March 2019 it ranked third in Iran for passenger traffic.
claims.why: Seven years stale and single-source; 2026 traffic is dominated by the war.

claims.claim: planned before 1979 when Mehrabad was congested
claims.wasBefore: It was planned before the 1979 revolution, when Mehrabad was already congested
claims.why: Only Wikipedia. VOA (February 2004) says construction began about 30 years earlier, which is not the same claim.

claims.claim: due to open May 2004 under a Turkish and Austrian consortium
claims.wasBefore: was due to open in May 2004 under a Turkish and Austrian consortium
claims.why: The consortium has one saveable source (Arabian Business and the Washington Post refused the fetcher). The May 2004 first day is kept with Reuters.

claims.claim: IRGC shut it days after first landing, citing security fears about foreigners
claims.wasBefore: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps shut it down days after the first landing, citing security fears about foreigners running the airport.
claims.why: Wrong on timing: both sources put it on the first day. The stated reason has one source. Replaced by the corrected sentence.

claims.wasBefore: It reopened in April 2005 with four Iranian airlines.
